title: Adaptive Prefill Thresholder and Kernel Scout to reduce tail latency
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: Sporadic tail latency spikes remain in production for mixed-content workloads. Investigation shows two correlated contributors: (1) aggressive admission that builds large heterogeneous prefill batches which force kernel paths with poor memory locality, and (2) late kernel selection when decode begins, causing on-the-fly kernel switches that add jitter.

Goal: Implement a lightweight on-request 'Thresholder' that rejects/defers prefill admission when predicted kernel mismatch risk or memory pressure is high, paired with a low-overhead 'Kernel Scout' probe that quickly benchmarks candidate kernels at short horizons to inform prefill scheduling and preferentially pick latency-stable paths for tail-sensitive tenants. The feature should reduce 99.9th-token latency by at least 20% on mixed workloads without regressing median latency or throughput more than 5%.

Approach/Design:
- Admission Thresholder (prefill-side): compute a short vector of features per incoming request (token length, model variant, tenant SLA tier, recent kernel failure rate, KV cache hit estimate, entropy heuristic). Run a lightweight decision function (initially rule-based with thresholds, later an L1 logistic fallback) to classify requests into: immediate admission, delayed admission (hold for up to 30ms to coalesce with similar shape), or route-to-fallback-model (lower-cost quantized kernel).
- Kernel Scout (probe runner): schedule very short synthetic probe runs (1-2 prefill steps) on candidate kernels during idle cycles and after admission for high-risk batches. Maintain an exponentially decaying score per kernel per GPU that reflects observed latency variance and memory pressure. Use score to prefer kernels with low jitter when shaping batches for tail-sensitive SLAs.
- Prefill/Decode Scheduling Interaction: when a batch contains heterogeneous sequence-lengths or mixing of pinned vs unpinned model versions, the Thresholder will optionally split or delay low-priority members to allow kernel-stable grouping. Decode windowing will request kernel lock-in at prefill completion if Kernel Scout indicates a stable winner; otherwise decode uses guarded switching with pre-allocated warmup slots to avoid cold-switch spikes.

Acceptance criteria:
1) End-to-end E2E test harness demonstrates >=20% reduction in 99.9th-token latency on our synthetic mixed workload (see test spec).
2) No more than 5% negative impact on throughput for P1 tenants in 30-minute sustained runs.
3) Feature toggles to enable/disable Thresholder and Scout independently.
4) Observability: per-batch kernel score, admission decision tag, and TLS of requests visible in console and in metrics dashboards.

Rollout plan: Canary on staging GPUs -> internal prod for txn-100 tenants -> gradual ramp to 20% of traffic (48h) -> monitor SLOs and canary metrics -> full rollout if stable.

Non-goals: full ML-based admission policy (we will iterate after a stable rule-based first pass), any changes to user-visible API surface, or persistent per-request user profiling beyond short decay windows.
comments: 2026-03-02 - Aisha: Spike showed kernel switches add ~6-12ms variance in 99.9th; attached microbench (link) and heap traces. Concluded we need admission heuristics plus proactive kernel probing.

2026-03-05 - Diego: Implemented prototype Thresholder rules in runtime branch feature/prefill-thresholder. Rule set: delay if (seq_len < 32 AND recent_kernel_switches > 0.1) OR (tenant_tier != premium AND kv_cache_hit < 0.2). Microbench locally shows 15% tail improvement in single-GPU sim.
2026-03-07 - Kiran (SRE): Observed elevated mem-pressure for heavy attention heads when batches mix long and short contexts. Suggested tracking GPU mem watermark and exposing it to Thresholder.

2026-03-09 - Diego: Added Kernel Scout prototype (uses 2-step probe on idle stream). Initial scoring uses EWMA of 99th latency; probe overhead <0.8% of cycles. Metrics pipeline: kernel.scout.score and kernel.scout.probes.count emitted to Prometheus (dashboard draft: https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/abc123/kernel-scout).

2026-03-11 - PM review (Riley): Concern about extra probes increasing overall GPU utilization; asked for a limit of max 2 probes per GPU per second and aggressive backoff when mem_pressure > 0.7. Added to TODO.

2026-03-13 - Diego: Run on canary cluster for 12h against mixed-production trace (trace id: trace_20260313_mix01). Results: 99.9th latency down 23% for target tenants, median unchanged, throughput -1.8%. Two incidents where Scout incorrectly preferred a quantized path leading to minor quality regression; rolled back Scout selection for pinned model versions. Issue tracked as ENG-770195.

2026-03-14 - Aisha: Security asked whether kernel probe payloads contain customer data — confirmed probes use synthetic tokens and do not touch customer KV caches. Security review not required but we logged the design in Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.internal/display/RIN/ENG-770193.
next_steps: 1) Finalize rule thresholds and add mem_watermark signal (Diego). 2) Add warmup-slot guarded kernel switching to decode path (Diego + Kiran). 3) Run extended 72h stress canary and validate against production traces (Aisha). 4) Prepare rollout runbook and feature flags (SRE).
